newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Trading perks up on Ivorian bourse, indices up.
newsitem.headline: Trading perks up on Ivorian bourse, indices up.

text.p: Trading on Ivory Coast's stock exchange, the Bourse des Valeurs d'Abidjan (BVA), perked up in the week to Friday, with textile company UNIWAX the biggest riser, its market report showed.

The BVA All-Share Index rose 0.68 percent to 356.29 points from 353.89 in the previous week, taking the 1996 rise to 28.51 percent. The 12VB 12-share index rose 1.5 percent to 241.07 points from 237.5, taking the 1996 rise to 20.98 percent.
Volume rose to 56,025,000 CFA francs from 37,538,000 CFA. The number of shares traded rose to 2,390 from 1,583. August is a holiday season among businesses in Ivory Coast.

UNIWAX (+3610 CFA to 55,000 CFA), food company NESTLE-CI (+2,340 CFA to 48,090 CFA), sack maker FILTISAC (+2,170 CFA to 44,570 CFA) and water supply company SODECI (+1,310 CFA to 22,000 CFA) were the risers.
The main faller was tobacco company SITAB (-2,250 CFA to 42,150 CFA).
The bourse, founded in 1976, recorded a 78.57 percent rise in market capitalisation to 400 billion CFA francs in 1995. Turnover was seven billion CFA, up from 6.4 billion in 1994.
The BVA index stood at 277.25 points at the end of 1995, up 115 percent on 1994. The 12VB at 199.26 points, up 64.01 percent on 1994.
